text:
nora_sales: Customer (regulated payroll) wants Private Deploy POC. Requirements: PrivateLink isolation, AZ-HA, TGW/BGP as failover to on-prem, monthly EIP rotation, and must correlate original client IPs in our auth logs. They asked for a one-paragraph netops blurb + firewall snippet and a short security checklist. Can we get that ready today?

ben_neteng: Short take: PrivateLink = interface endpoints (ENIs) and it NATs client traffic -> original src IP is not visible to our backend. Options to surface identity: (A) in-VPC egress proxy that inserts X-Forwarded-For or a custom header; (B) use PROXY protocol between their proxy and our edge so we see the true TCP source IP; (C) route via TGW with a customer NAT EIP (if they can supply static EIP/BYOIP) so logs show the known NAT IP. If they require cryptographic identity, mTLS + client certs is best.

kai_arch: Infra notes: create one VPCE per AZ and front with a tiny HA proxy fleet (active-active). Enable PrivateLink private DNS so service FQDN resolves to ENI IPs. For cross-region, either replicate endpoints or use inter-region TGW. BGP failover pattern: prefer VPCE-local routes; TGW BGP advertised prefixes as secondary with higher administrative distance.

leila_infosec: Security checklist (paste-ready):
- Provide KMS key policy + retention window for audit logs; confirm TLS mode (mTLS preferred) and cert rotation cadence.
- Agree EIP rotation cadence and maintenance windows; provide automation for firewall updates or accept FQDN-based allowlist with documented TTL expectations.

ben_neteng: Firewall snippet for their network team (egress rules) - replace placeholders:
```
# allow egress to Redwood POC endpoints
allow tcp from 10.200.0.0/16 to 3.115.210.99/32 port 443
# for PrivateLink enable access to VPCE ENIs or security-group
allow tcp from 10.200.0.0/16 to vpce-06b7c8d9e0f1 443
# allow our health probes
allow tcp from 10.200.0.0/16 <- 15.80.45.0/24 443
```
Note: If they perform TLS inspection and rewrite SNI, recommend mTLS or PROXY protocol; X-Forwarded-For can be used if their proxy inserts it and they trust header provenance.

nora_sales: Can someone hand me a 3-line netops blurb and a 2-line security checklist I can paste into their ticket? They want kickoff in 9 business days.

ben_neteng: 3-line netops handoff for their ops: 
- Provision PrivateLink interface endpoints in every AZ for low-latency; front endpoints with HA proxies and enable PrivateLink private DNS.
- PrivateLink NATs client IP; to preserve original src IP run an in-VPC egress proxy that inserts X-Forwarded-For or use PROXY protocol to our edge, or route via TGW with a customer NAT EIP if BYOIP is possible.
- Open outbound TCP/443 to assigned EIP(s) or VPCE IDs; monthly EIP rotation requires a scheduled maintenance window and automation to update firewall rules. Expect per-endpoint hourly + per-GB data processing charges.

leila_infosec: 2-line infosec checklist (ready to paste):
- Provide KMS key policy for audit logs and confirm TLS mode (mTLS preferred) with cert rotation cadence.
- Confirm monthly EIP rotation schedule and maintenance window; provide automation for firewall updates or accept DNS/FQDN-based allowlist and note expected TTLs.

netbot: netbot: Created ticket POC-77412-net-handoff and assigned to #eng-infra; owner: ben_neteng; ETA: 4 business days.

kai_arch: Blockers before we provision: their network diagram, expected monthly egress GB, peak RPS, whether they rewrite SNI, and if they can provide automation for EIP churn. If they share those, we can stand up test endpoints in ~48h.

nora_sales: I'll upload the diagram + traffic estimate to POC-77412 today. Thanks all! :white_check_mark:
